Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 FY2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 FY2025 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Lisa Wong, CTO; David Kim, Chief Revenue Officer; Emma Rodriguez, Chief Product Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Marketing Officer; and Taylor Brooks, Chief Customer Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 FY2025. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge AI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on eight key areas: gross margin expansion, customer mix evolution, product roadmap progress, LTV/CAC ratio strengthening, CAC trends improvement, free cash flow generation, NRR performance, and churn analysis.

Let me start with our product roadmap, where we've made tremendous strides, accelerating our transition from a core collaboration platform to a full-stack workflow orchestration suite. This positions us squarely in the massive SaaS market, where leaders are seeing high NRRs through AI-driven expansions.

We rolled out CloudForge AI Predict, our generative AI-powered workflow forecasting engine, integrated natively with our platform. Leveraging large language models fine-tuned on billions of anonymized interactions from our customer base, it delivers exceptional accuracy in predictions. Early adopters have seen major reductions in variance, translating to incremental ARR from upsells. Customer satisfaction is high, with strong activation rates among enterprise users.

Building on that, we launched CloudForge Flows 2.0, our low-code workflow automation builder with composable modules. It supports hundreds of pre-built connectors to tools like Slack, Zoom, Snowflake, and more. Adoption has been explosive, especially in SMBs, boosting MRR and dropping churn.

Our top priority is CloudForge One, our unified agentic AI platform set for general availability soon. This autonomous platform handles end-to-end workflows, powered by advanced RAG architecture and multi-modal inputs. Pilots show faster cycles and higher win rates. We're investing heavily in R&D to make AI a major part of our ARR.

We're also advancing enterprise-grade security with CloudForge Shield, including zero-trust, compliance certifications, and AI-driven threat detection. This is gaining traction in financial services.

Regionally, North America leads growth, EMEA benefits from compliance focus, APAC surges with local integrations, and emerging markets get localized versions.

This roadmap powers our platform flywheel, with a growing app marketplace and strong ROI focus. We're raising guidance accordingly.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail, including deep dives into our other key focus areas.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $598 million, representing a 24% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82.5%, and operating income was $120 million.

Moving to our gross margin performance, which continues to reflect the scalability and efficiency inherent in our multi-tenant SaaS architecture—a hallmark of leading players like Snowflake and ServiceNow.

For Q3 FY2025, we delivered a non-GAAP gross margin of 82.5%, up 130 basis points sequentially from 81.2% in Q2 and 270 basis points year-over-year from 79.8% in Q3 FY2024. On a GAAP basis, gross margin was 81.1%, compared to 79.8% in Q2 and 78.5% a year ago, with the GAAP-non-GAAP difference primarily driven by $4.2 million in stock-based compensation and amortization of developed technology, in line with our capitalization policy under ASC 350-40.

Let me break down the drivers of this expansion, starting with the sequential improvement. The 130 basis point lift was fueled by three key levers.

First, hosting and infrastructure cost optimizations, which accounted for roughly 60% of the gain. We completed the rollout of our GenAI-powered resource orchestration platform across 85% of our production workloads. This initiative dynamically scales compute and storage using predictive analytics on usage patterns—similar to how Datadog leverages AI for observability. As a result, we reduced average server costs by 18% quarter-over-quarter, particularly on AWS Graviton4 instances and Google Cloud's TPUs for our ML inference workloads. This shaved about 90 basis points off cost of revenue as a percentage of ARR.

Second, improved customer mix and self-serve adoption. Our Enterprise segment, now 62% of total ARR, up from 58% YoY, carries a blended gross margin of 85%, benefiting from land-and-expand dynamics where we upsell premium modules like our AI Copilot for workflow automation. Conversely, self-serve SMB cohorts expanded to 28% of net new ARR, with margins above 90% due to minimal support touchpoints. This shift offset some pricing pressure in EMEA, where we introduced volume discounts for our CloudForge Teams product to compete with Microsoft Teams' bundling aggression.

Third, foreign exchange and regional efficiencies. Americas revenue, 65% of total, held steady at 84% margins, but APAC—now 15% of ARR—saw a 200 basis point improvement to 78% as we localized data centers in Singapore and Sydney, reducing latency-related egress fees by 22%. This follows our $50 million capex commitment last year to edge computing, mirroring MongoDB's strategy in hyperscale regions.

Year-over-year, the 270 basis point expansion reflects the maturity of our platform. Back in Q3 FY2024, we were ramping investments in GPU clusters for our initial AI features, which inflated COGS by 3 points due to higher NVIDIA A100 rental rates amid the chip shortage. Today, with H100s normalized and our custom Kubernetes operators optimizing pod density by 35%, those costs have normalized. Additionally, support and professional services costs declined 15% as a percentage of revenue, thanks to our Knowledge Graph-powered chatbots handling 70% of L1 tickets—putting us on par with Zendesk's automation benchmarks.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 gross margins to land in the 82% to 83% range, with upside from further AI efficiencies and downside risk limited to 50 basis points from incremental R&D hosting for our upcoming Federated Learning module. Strategically, we're prioritizing margin accretion through three pillars: annual infrastructure RFPs, targeting 10-15% savings like our recent Azure hybrid deal; product-led growth to boost self-serve mix to 35% by FY2026; and zero-trust security investments to preempt compliance costs under GDPR 2.0 and upcoming SEC cybersecurity rules.

This positions us at the high end of SaaS peers—our Rule of 55 score now at 62, with gross margins sustainably above 80% supporting 25%+ free cash flow margins long-term.

I'll now dive into our customer mix dynamics, which continue to be a key driver of our predictable revenue model and long-term growth trajectory here at CloudForge. As a reminder, we categorize our customers into two primary segments: Enterprise, which includes Fortune 1000 and equivalent global large enterprises with ACV typically north of $100,000; and SMB, encompassing small and medium businesses with ACV generally ranging from $5,000 to $50,000. This bifurcation helps us track our land-and-expand strategy, where we start with point solutions in collaboration, workflow automation, and AI-driven insights, then expand into full-suite deployments akin to how Slack evolved into Salesforce's enterprise powerhouse or how Atlassian's Jira scaled from SMB dev teams to Fortune 500 program management.

Turning to Q3 results, our overall customer mix showed meaningful progress toward enterprise balance. Enterprise revenue represented 62% of total ARR—up from 55% a year ago and 58% in Q2—while SMB contributed the remaining 38%. This shift drove our blended ACV to $68,400, a 22% YoY increase, with Enterprise ACV averaging $142,000—boosted by multi-year deals averaging 3.2 years in duration—and SMB ACV at $18,700, which held steady sequentially but grew 12% YoY on pricing optimization.

Customer count tells a complementary story: We added 1,240 net new customers in the quarter, with 210 in Enterprise—a 35% YoY acceleration—and 1,030 in SMB, which grew 18% YoY but at a decelerating pace due to our deliberate focus on higher-LTV logos. Enterprise seat expansion was particularly robust, with existing customers adding 28% more seats quarter-over-quarter, pushing our Dollar-Based Net Retention—or NRR—to 118% for Enterprise, compared to 112% for SMB. This land-and-expand motion mirrors industry leaders like ServiceNow, where workflow orchestration starts small but scales to platform-wide adoption.

Regionally, the trends vary but reinforce our global diversification. In the Americas, which account for 68% of ARR, Enterprise mix hit 68%—up 450 basis points YoY—fueled by hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure, where we're embedding our AI co-pilot for real-time collaboration analytics into their marketplaces. EMEA, at 22% of ARR, saw Enterprise rise to 55% from 48% YoY, driven by GDPR-compliant features and wins in financial services; think Deutsche Bank-scale deployments for compliant teamspaces. APAC, our fastest-growing region at 10% of ARR, remains SMB-heavy at 65% mix but flipped positive with 15 new Enterprise logos, including two telcos in Japan leveraging our low-latency edge integrations amid rising demand for hybrid work tools post the Zoom fatigue era.

Strategically, these shifts aren't accidental—they stem from three key initiatives. First, our Enterprise Edition, with federated SSO, SOC 2 Type II, and ML-powered security incident response, has shortened sales cycles from 120 to 85 days for deals over $250k ACV, much like Zoom's pivot to enterprise post-IPO. Second, we've doubled down on a dedicated Enterprise sales force—now 40% of our quota-carrying reps—paired with ABM campaigns targeting CISOs and CROs, yielding a 3x ROI on CAC versus SMB self-serve. Third, technical investments in our GraphQL API and no-code workflow builder have enabled 40% of Enterprise expansions, allowing seamless integrations with Salesforce Einstein, Microsoft Power Platform, and Workday—addressing the multi-tool sprawl that's plaguing 70% of SaaS stacks per Gartner.

Looking forward, we expect Enterprise to reach 65-67% of ARR by year-end, supported by a $2.1B pipeline that's 3.8x our Q4 quota and 68% Enterprise-weighted. This mix evolution enhances margin expansion—Enterprise gross margins at 84% versus SMB's 79%—while mitigating macro headwinds like SMB budget scrutiny amid 4-5% U.S. unemployment forecasts. SMB remains vital for top-of-funnel innovation testing and 20-25% YoY cohort growth, but Enterprise predictability positions us for 28-30% revenue growth in FY26, in line with high-end SaaS peers like Snowflake or Datadog.

Next, on our LTV to CAC ratio, a cornerstone metric for any SaaS business like ours here at CloudForge, where we deliver AI-powered collaboration and analytics platforms to enterprise teams—think a blend of Slack's real-time workflows with Tableau's data insights, but supercharged for mid-market and Fortune 1000 scalability.

For Q3 FY2025, our LTV/CAC ratio came in at 4.2x, up from 3.8x in Q2 and a robust improvement over the 3.4x we reported a year ago. This puts us firmly in the elite tier of SaaS benchmarks—Bessemer Venture Partners' latest State of the Cloud report pegs the median for public SaaS at around 3.5x, with top performers like Snowflake and HubSpot pushing 4.5x-plus on the strength of high net retention and efficient go-to-market engines. At CloudForge, this 4.2x reflects not just payback period compression to under 14 months but also our ability to generate sustainable free cash flow as we scale toward our Rule of 40 target of 45% this fiscal year.

Lifetime Value (LTV): Our cohort-based LTV stands at $45,200 per customer, calculated as Average ARR of $14,800 multiplied by our gross margin of 82%, divided by annualized churn of 4.8%. That's a $2,400 QoQ lift, driven primarily by our NRR climbing to 118% from 114% last quarter. Expansions are firing on all cylinders: 42% of our customer base upsold or cross-sold in Q3, fueled by our new AI Agent Builder module, which automates 30% of routine analytics tasks and has sticky adoption rates north of 75% among early adopters. Gross margin held steady at 82% despite R&D investments in edge computing integrations, thanks to our AWS partnership optimizing infra costs to sub-18% of revenue.

Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC): CAC clocked in at $10,800—a 12% sequential decline and 22% better YoY. Breaking out the blend: Paid channels represent 38% of CAC at $4,100, down due to a 28% improvement in our multi-touch attribution model's paid efficiency—ROAS now at 5.2x versus 4.1x last year. Sales & marketing as a percentage of ARR dropped to 28% from 32%, with outbound SDR-led motions for enterprise deals averaging $18K CAC but paying back in 9 months via $60K+ ACV logos. Inbound and product-led growth channels crushed it at $6,200 CAC, comprising 62% of new logos, as our freemium self-serve tier—now with viral coefficients of 1.3 from team sharing—drove 65K signups, converting 22% to paid within 90 days.

Trends and Cohort Insights: Looking at vintages, our Q1 FY24 cohort has matured to a 4.8x LTV/CAC today, validating the step-function improvement from PLG investments we made post-2022 macro headwinds. YoY, LTV expanded 18% on churn compression, while CAC fell 22% as we shifted mix toward high-velocity SMB deals which now represent 55% of bookings but only 35% of CAC dollars. This mirrors playbook successes at companies like Notion or Atlassian, where PLG has redefined scalable acquisition in a high-interest-rate world.

Regional Commentary: Geographically, the U.S. remains our powerhouse at 5.1x LTV/CAC, buoyed by 125% YoY ARR growth in verticals like financial services, where compliance-ready AI features have landed deals with three bulge-bracket banks. EMEA improved sharply to 3.7x from 3.1x, as GDPR-aligned data sovereignty zones and localized pricing reduced sales cycles by 25%—EMEA now 22% of total ARR. APAC is the growth wildcard at 3.2x, up from 2.6x, with Japan and Australia cohorts hitting breakeven payback in 16 months thanks to partnerships with SoftBank and telcos; however, China regulatory hurdles cap us at 5% mix for now, so we're doubling down on Singapore hub expansions.

Technical Initiatives Driving This: Under the hood, our engineering team's Q3 wins include a 40% reduction in onboarding friction via no-code API connectors to Salesforce and Workday, boosting Day 30 retention to 92%. We've also rolled out predictive churn models using our own platform's ML stack, intervening on 15% of at-risk accounts and recovering $2.3M in ARR. On the acquisition front, A/B testing of personalized demo flows via Gong-integrated sales AI cut CAC by 16% for mid-market.

Strategic Insights and Outlook: This 4.2x positions us to weather any macro storm—our LTV/CAC Rule of 40 contribution is now +32 points to growth. Strategically, we're leaning into land-and-expand with cohort-based expansion pods targeting 125% NRR by FY26, while pruning low-LTV channels like broad SEM in favor of community-led growth. Looking forward, we expect Q4 at 4.4x-4.6x as APAC scales and enterprise motion matures, with sensitivity to forex but insulated by 85% dollar-denominated ARR.

Turning to customer acquisition cost trends, which continue to reflect the efficiency gains we're driving across our go-to-market engine. As a reminder, we define CAC as our total sales and marketing expenses—encompassing paid media, content, events, sales team compensation, and partner commissions—divided by the number of new customers added in the period. We're laser-focused on optimizing this metric, targeting a sub-12-month payback period and a sustainable LTV-to-CAC ratio above 4x, which aligns with top-quartile SaaS performers like those tracked in Bessemer Venture Partners' State of the Cloud reports.

For Q3 FY2025, our dollar-based CAC came in at $428, marking an 18% sequential decline from $520 in Q2 and a robust 28% year-over-year improvement from $595 in Q3 FY2024. This puts us well ahead of our internal guidance of 15-20% YoY reduction, driven by a combination of channel mix shifts, product-led growth acceleration, and disciplined spend management amid moderating macro headwinds.

Channel-Level Trends and Initiatives: Performance Marketing (45% of new ACV): CAC here dropped 25% QoQ to $320, thanks to refined Google Ads and LinkedIn campaigns leveraging our new AI-powered audience segmentation tool—similar to how HubSpot has scaled its inbound flywheel. We've reduced cost-per-lead by 22% through better negative keyword targeting and lookalike audiences built on anonymized first-party data from our customer base. ROAS now exceeds 5x, up from 3.8x a year ago.

PLG and Organic (30% of new ACV): This is our lowest-CAC channel at $185, surging 35% QoQ in contribution as we rolled out freemium tiers inspired by Notion and Miro. Our viral coefficient hit 1.3 in Q3, fueled by in-app referral loops and Slack integrations that drive bottom-up adoption in SMBs. Self-serve conversions now account for 42% of new logos, compressing sales cycles from 45 to 28 days.

Direct Sales and Partnerships (25% of new ACV): Enterprise CAC remains higher at $850 but with improving payback—now 11 months versus 14 last year—via targeted Account-Based Marketing plays. Key wins include co-sell partnerships with AWS Marketplace and Salesforce AppExchange, mirroring Snowflake's ecosystem strategy, which lowered partner-attributed CAC by 15% through revenue shares.

Regional Commentary: North America (72% of ARR): CAC at $385, our most efficient market, down 20% YoY. EMEA (18% of ARR): $510 CAC, improved 12% QoQ despite regulatory hurdles. APAC (10% of ARR): Highest at $680, but trending down 10% YoY as we scale Japan and India teams.

Efficiency Metrics and Strategic Insights: CAC Payback Period: Compressed to 9.2 months in Q3, the fastest in our history. LTV:CAC Ratio: 4.5x overall. Forward Initiatives: We're investing in AI-driven personalization to further de-leverage CAC by 15-20%, expanding marketplaces, and balancing channel mix. These improvements directly fuel our Rule of 50 trajectory.

On free cash flow, which continues to underscore the durability and scalability of our SaaS model.

For the quarter, we generated $48.2 million in free cash flow, representing a robust 28% year-over-year increase from $37.6 million in Q3 FY2024. On a trailing twelve-month basis, FCF reached $192 million, up 35% YoY, with FCF margins expanding to 32% of revenue—well ahead of our peer group average.

Free cash flow is cash from operations minus CapEx. Our operating cash flow came in at $52.1 million, up 32% YoY, driven by record revenue. CapEx remained disciplined at $3.9 million, or 0.7% of revenue.

Key drivers: Operational Efficiency and Cash Conversion Cycle Improvements: Cycle shortened to 28 days, DSO to 51 days. Non-cash expenses added tailwind. Gross margins at 81%.

Sales and Marketing Efficiency: PLG reduced CAC, payback to 14 months, LTV:CAC 3.2x.

R&D Discipline: Optimized spend through cloud-native tech.

Challenges: Some SMB churn and APAC investments, but offset.

Regional: Strong Americas, growing EMEA and APAC.

Outlook: Q4 FCF $52-56 million, path to 40% margins by FY2026.

Moving to net revenue retention, or NRR, which remains a cornerstone of our SaaS flywheel. For Q3 FY2025, we delivered an NRR of 118%, marking our 11th straight quarter above 110% and accelerating 300 basis points year-over-year from 115%. This underscores the stickiness of our platform.

NRR calculation: Gross retention 95%, logo churn 3.2% annualized, contraction 1.8%.

Churn at 3.2%, low end of peers, driven by ForgeGuard health scoring.

Contraction minimal at 1.8%, thanks to usage-based pricing.

Expansion at 23%, from seats, upsells, cross-sells.

Expect 117-120% in Q4.

Finally, on churn metrics, which remain a cornerstone of our SaaS health. Overall annual logo churn held steady at 4.2% in Q3, down from 5.1% a year ago, while gross dollar retention improved to 92% from 88% YoY.

NRR expanded to 118%, driven by 28% expansion.

Primary Drivers: SMB contraction 62% of churn at 7.8%; feature gaps 18%; onboarding friction 12%; macro 8%.

Mitigation: AI-powered ForgeGuard with 87% precision, recovering ARR; ForgeFast onboarding; pricing optimization; regional partnerships.

PLG reduces low-usage churn. Expect GDR 94% by year-end.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $2.3 billion to $2.4 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Wong for a technology update.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Emma Rodriguez will provide update on product roadmap.

Emma Rodriguez:
Thank you, Lisa. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of AI Copilot. This new feature significantly improves workflow productivity by 40%. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Emma. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 25% increase in website traffic and a 30% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jordan. We are committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences and this quarter, we focused on improving our customer support and onboarding processes. As a result, we have seen a 15% increase in customer satisfaction scores.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge AI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, what's the competitive landscape like, and how do you plan to differentiate yourselves?

David Kim:
Thanks, Ben. CloudForge AI has been a major growth driver, contributing over 30% of new ARR this quarter through upsells and new logos. Attach rates are at 45% among eligible customers, exceeding our initial expectations by 15 points due to the immediate productivity gains. The competitive landscape includes players like Microsoft Teams and Zoom, but we differentiate with deep AI workflow orchestration, seamless integrations, and superior enterprise security features that lock in land-and-expand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley.

Maria Lopez:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, what are your expected ROI from these investments, and what are the key challenges you anticipate?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Maria. We're accelerating international expansion with heavy focus on APAC, where we've localized data centers and integrations. Key targets are Japan, Southeast Asia telcos and fintechs. We expect 3x ROI within two years from these investments, based on current pilots. Challenges include regulatory hurdles like data sovereignty and local competition, but our edge partnerships and compliance toolkit position us well.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, what's the impact of pricing changes on churn, and what are your long-term targets for NRR?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Raj. As detailed earlier, churn is stable at 4.2% annualized logos, with NRR trending up to 118%. Strategies include AI predictive tools like ForgeGuard, personalized onboarding, and PLG enhancements—reducing at-risk accounts significantly. Pricing changes have had neutral to positive impact, with freemium tiers boosting retention. Long-term, we're targeting 120%+ NRR by FY2026 through expansion focus.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays.

Lisa Chen:
Can you provide more color on customer acquisition costs (CAC) and payback periods for new customers?

Mike Patel:
Sure, Lisa. As covered, blended CAC is around $10,800 per customer, with dollar-based at $428—down significantly YoY. Payback periods have compressed to 9-12 months overall, 9 months for PLG, thanks to efficiency gains and strong NRR.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
